newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean union body vows to step up strikes.
newsitem.headline: South Korean union body vows to step up strikes.

text.p: South Korea's most militant union body on Tuesday vowed to intensify strikes after President Kim Young-sam ignored its demands to scrap a controversial new labour law.

"We have no choice but to intensify our strikes," Kwon Young-il, president of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions told a news conference, hours after Kim threw his weight behind the legislation that allows companies to shed workers.

Kwon said his outlawed union body, which claims 500,000 members, would advance plans to bring out public sector workers on subways and in telecommunication companies, including state-owned Korea Telecom. He gave no timetable.
He called for an alliance with the traditionally more moderate Federation of Korean Trade Unions, which boasts 1.2 million members, to fight the new law.
The federation has ordered a walkout by its members starting on Saturday.

"We are saddened that the president, who should be in charge of governing the nation, does not know the seriousness of this crisis," Kwon said. Kim earlier told a news conference the new law was needed to boost South Korea's global competitiveness.
